narration: If you shopped online today on your iPhone, you might've paid 30% more than the person next to you — for the exact same item. It's called dynamic pricing, and it's 100% legal.
visual: Two smartphones side by side — iPhone showing hotel room at $234, Android showing same room at $189. Both phones slide in from opposite sides. Alert badge pops in: 'SAME ROOM. SAME NIGHT.'

narration: Amazon alone changes its prices two and a half million times every single day. Algorithms look at your device, your location, and your browsing history to decide what to charge you.
visual: Animated counter rapidly counting up to 2,500,000 on dark display. Bar chart below shows volatile price history for one item — alternating red and green bars revealing left to right.

narration: Studies found Mac and iPhone users get shown prices up to 30% higher on the same hotels and flights. Orbitz was literally caught hiding cheaper rooms from Apple users back in 2012.
visual: Large '30%' percentage counts up on dark background with 'MORE' beside it. Fact card slides up showing the Orbitz Wall Street Journal story as source.

narration: Visit a product page three times and the algorithm flags you as interested — then bumps the price. Researchers documented markups as high as 15% just for repeat visits.
visual: Three browser windows appear in sequence: Visit #1 shows $287, Visit #2 shows $304, Visit #3 shows $329. Arrow between each visit. Cookie icon with red X appears at bottom.

narration: The fix is dead simple: open an incognito window, clear your cookies, or use a VPN before any big purchase. This tiny habit saves shoppers between $200 and $800 every single year.
visual: Three green cards slide in stacked vertically: incognito glasses icon, cookie with X icon, VPN shield icon. Green savings badge springs in: '$200–$800/YEAR'.

narration: The algorithm knows your shopping habits better than you do — and it's pricing accordingly. Follow for more traps they don't want you to catch.
visual: Three dark stat tiles appear showing key numbers: 2.5M, 30%, $200–$800. Large red FOLLOW button springs in at the bottom of the screen.
